about.title: North Hollywood Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: North Hollywood's mix of dense apartment buildings, retail corridors, and busy sidewalks along Lankershim and Vineland means people are constantly moving through spaces someone else maintains. When a property owner or manager lets a hazard sit unaddressed — a wet tile floor, a broken stair rail, cracked pavement outside a strip mall, poor lighting in a parking structure — the results can be serious. California law asks whether the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the danger and failed to fix it or warn people. That's why documenting the scene matters so much: photos of the hazard, witness names, and a request to preserve any surveillance footage can shape the entire claim. We handle premises liability cases directly and work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Documentation Matters in a North Hollywood Fall Claim

items.title: Notice Has to Be Shown
items.desc: California requires proof the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard before your fall. We can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records to establish that timeline.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many North Hollywood businesses and apartment buildings recycle surveillance footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having evidence and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're found partly responsible for not noticing a hazard, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows recovery — reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated by it.

items.question: I fell at a store near the NoHo Arts District — what should I do first?
items.answer: If you're able, photograph the exact spot, any spill or debris, and the surrounding area before it's cleaned up. Ask an employee to file an incident report and get the names of anyone who saw it happen. Then reach out to us for a free case review so we can request the store's surveillance footage before it's overwritten.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit, though claims against a public entity — like a city-owned sidewalk or building — often carry a much shorter deadline. Because that timeline can be easy to miss, it's worth having us review the details early.

items.question: What if the property owner says I wasn't paying attention?
items.answer: That argument comes up often, but it doesn't automatically defeat a claim. California's comparative fault system allows for recovery even if you're found partially at fault, with the amount adjusted accordingly. We can help evaluate the specific facts and push back on unfair blame-shifting.
